TO THE 18-YEAR-OLD PACKING HIS BAG
I LEFT HOME AT 18.
TEN YEARS LATER —
HERE'S THE INVOICE NOBODY SHOWED ME.
2 / 7
Tap to follow →
→
Save this ↓
WHAT NOBODY TELLS YOU

The fighting was supposed to fade by 25.

It didn't. It just lowered its voice. Technology moved faster in my twenties than in my parents' whole adult lives — I sprinted, they couldn't keep pace. That gap isn't malice. It's math.

3 / 7
Tap to follow →
→
Save this ↓
THE TRADE NOBODY WARNS YOU ABOUT

My parents gave me an education expensive enough to show me every life I could have had — and not one thing to do with the seeing.

Exposure is irreversible. The door doesn't close. It stands open behind you, letting in a draft.

THE DREAM THAT WASN'T MINE

My "dream" of computer science wasn't a dream. It was the only shape available.

Then I met people carrying ambitions I'd never been offered. I caught them like a fever. Still chasing — every time I get close, the finish line moves.

5 / 7

WHAT TEN YEARS ACTUALLY BUILT

Underneath the ambition was always love wearing a work costume.

Loneliness, most waking hours. Walls I called impenetrable. A few people got through anyway. That's the whole ledger — and a few turned out to be enough.

6 / 7
Tap to follow →

Save this ↓
THE THESIS

Independence doesn't cost you your family. It costs you the version of yourself that could have been satisfied.

You don't find out which life you preferred until you're too far in to test it. I'd still go.
